learningObjectives: Describe and reproduce sliding and turning motions informally and precisely
Identify rays/angles that differ and defend more than one valid odd-one-out
Describe all three six-frame triangle dances to a partner using clear slide amount/direction and turn amount/direction
Invert a dance by reversing ordered moves, retaining exact magnitudes and reversing turn direction

studentModes.prompt: Among original four common-vertex ray pairs A straight 180°, B right 90°, C acute 45°, D obtuse 125°, choose one that does not belong AND defend with an accurate mathematical property. Multiple defensible choices exist.
studentModes.acceptance: Use any mathematically valid differentiator; e.g. A is the only 180°, B the only right angle, C the only acute, D the only obtuse. Do not auto-grade letter alone.
studentModes.negative: A choice without property or with demonstrably wrong angle classification is insufficient.

studentModes.prompt: Secretly choose Edulytiks first-party A/B/C six-frame dance cards; describe the complete directed slides and quarter-turns without naming the card. Partner reconstructs and identifies it, then switch roles.
studentModes.correctness: A/B first slide right 2; both turn 90° clockwise next; C turns 90° counterclockwise; A and B diverge at frame 4. All preserve an asymmetric triangle's lengths/angles.
studentModes.negative: Only naming A/B/C, omitting a frame or confusing clockwise/counterclockwise is insufficient.

studentModes.prompt: Choose one A/B/C sequence. Start at frame 6 and describe inverse moves in reverse order.
studentModes.correctness: Reverse every slide by same distance opposite direction; inverse of clockwise turn is counterclockwise of equal angle, and vice versa; undo move 5→6 before move 4→5.
studentModes.negative: Reversing the list of directions without inverting each movement is incorrect.

studentModes.prompt: An asymmetrical triangle has marked P=(1,1), tip north. Slide right 3, then turn clockwise 90° around the new P. Draw/describe final pose, final P and tip direction and why sides/angles remain unchanged.

rubric.expected: P ends at (4,1), the marked tip points east after a clockwise quarter-turn; no side length or angle measure changes

criteria.name: Congruent figure preserving lengths and angles

rubric.scale: 0 incorrect/missing, 1 partially justified, 2 correct with evidence

studentModes.evidence: teacher stores descriptive criterion notes and four scores, 0–2 each; 8 maximum, not numeric auto-grading

coordinateQuestionCandidate.scopeLimit: Only fixed-point translation coordinate, not substitute for ray/partner/dance/human work
coordinateQuestionCandidate.prompt: P=(1,1) translated right 3 units: report P′
coordinateQuestionCandidate.algorithm: translate x by +3, y unchanged; canonicalize signed zero and decimal equivalents
coordinateQuestionCandidate.parser: Trim, optional outer parentheses, exactly two finite base-10 signed decimals separated by comma, whitespace allowed; reject scientific notation, NaN, Infinity, extra coordinates and empty/null; limit numeric magnitude to safe finite range
boundary: (-0,1) is a valid parsed point but not the key
(4,-0) valid parsed point but not the key
(4,1.0000001) not equivalent to the exact answer
